entities.summary: The Royal Burgh of Haddington is a town in East Lothian, Scotland. It is the main administrative, cultural and geographical centre for East Lothian. It lies about 17 miles east of Edinburgh. The name Haddington is Anglo-Saxon, dating from the sixth or seventh century AD when the area was incorporated into the Kingdom of Bernicia. The town, like the rest of the Lothian region, was ceded by King Edgar of England and became part of Scotland in the tenth century. Haddington received Burgh status, one of the earliest to do so, during the reign of David I (1124–1153), giving it trading rights which encouraged its growth into a market town.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Haddington's Burgh status during David I's reign encouraged its growth into a market town, contributing to the regional economic development of East Lothian. This local administrative change had a lasting impact on the town's cultural and geographical significance.
